ambiguities.text: The term 'similar' for token name/symbol comparison is not precisely defined
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume similarity includes: exact match with different case, common typosquatting patterns (0 vs O, 1 vs l), and Levenshtein distance within threshold. Wallets should implement their own heuristics.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not define what happens if metadata download fails after returning true
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume wallet should gracefully handle metadata fetch failures by using placeholder values or not displaying the token until metadata is available.

ambiguities.text: The relationship between ERC1046 and legacy ERC20 types is not clearly specified
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume ERC1046 is the preferred type that provides tokenURI for metadata, while ERC20 type is legacy and requires explicit symbol/decimals/image in options.

implicit_assumptions.description: The dApp providing the token information is not necessarily trusted; all data must be verified by the wallet
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious dApps could trick users into tracking fake tokens that impersonate real assets

implicit_assumptions.description: The wallet has access to reliable token lists or registries to perform phishing detection
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Without reference data, wallets cannot detect token impersonation attacks

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers can create contracts with any symbol or name, making on-chain data alone insufficient for verification
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If this assumption is wrong (name/symbol are somehow trusted), wallets might over-rely on on-chain data

implicit_assumptions.description: Users understand the difference between tracking a token and owning/approving it
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Users might confuse wallet_watchAsset approval with transaction approval, leading to confusion about their actual holdings
